statement: Extended Kalman Filter. For the nonlinear system x_t = f(x_{t-1}, u_t, w_t), z_t = h(x_t, v_t), with w_t ~ N(0, Q_t) and v_t ~ N(0, R_t), linearize f around the previous posterior mean and h around the predicted mean using a first-order Taylor expansion. Then run the linear Kalman filter on the linearized model. Prediction: x̂_{t|t-1} = f(x̂_{t-1|t-1}, u_t, 0) and P_{t|t-1} = F_t P_{t-1|t-1} F_t^T + F_w Q_t F_w^T. Correction: K_t = P_{t|t-1} H_t^T (H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T + H_v R_t H_v^T)^{-1}, x̂_{t|t} = x̂_{t|t-1} + K_t (z_t − h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0)), and P_{t|t} = (I − K_t H_t) P_{t|t-1}. Here F_t = ∂f/∂x_{t-1} and F_w = ∂f/∂w_t, both evaluated at (x̂_{t-1|t-1}, w_t = 0). H_t = ∂h/∂x_t and H_v = ∂h/∂v_t, both evaluated at (x̂_{t|t-1}, v_t = 0). The mean is propagated through the full nonlinear f and h. Only the covariance and the gain use the Jacobians. When the noise is additive (F_w = I, H_v = I), these reduce to the textbook form K_k = P_{k|k-1} H_k^T (H_k P_{k|k-1} H_k^T + R_k)^{-1}. The sources already use the sheet notation (Q, R, P, F, H, K), so no symbols are renamed.

symbols.dimensions: R^n x R^l x R^q -> R^n

symbols.meaning: Jacobian of f with respect to the state, evaluated at x̂_{t-1|t-1}
Jacobian of f with respect to the process noise, evaluated at x̂_{t-1|t-1}, w_t = 0
Jacobian of h with respect to the state, evaluated at x̂_{t|t-1}
Jacobian of h with respect to the measurement noise, evaluated at x̂_{t|t-1}, v_t = 0
predicted (prior) mean and state error covariance
corrected (posterior) mean and state error covariance
effective input of the linearized motion model, f(x̂_{t-1|t-1}, u_t, 0) − F_t x̂_{t-1|t-1}
effective offset of the linearized observation model, h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0) − H_t x̂_{t|t-1}
posterior and predicted belief over x_t

steps.text: Start from the nonlinear models x_t = f(x_{t-1}, u_t, w_t) and z_t = h(x_t, v_t), with w_t ~ N(0, Q_t) and v_t ~ N(0, R_t) (eq. 30). The linear Kalman filter cannot be applied directly because f and h are not linear.

Take the first-order Taylor expansion of f about (x̂_{t-1|t-1}, w_t = 0) and of h about (x̂_{t|t-1}, v_t = 0) (eq. 31): x_t ≈ f(x̂_{t-1|t-1}, u_t, 0) + F_t (x_{t-1} − x̂_{t-1|t-1}) + F_w w_t, and z_t ≈ h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0) + H_t (x_t − x̂_{t|t-1}) + H_v v_t. The expansion point for h is the predicted mean, not the previous posterior mean.

The coefficients are Jacobians evaluated at the expansion points (eqs. 32–33): F_t = ∂f/∂x_{t-1} at x̂_{t-1|t-1}; F_w = ∂f/∂w_t at (x̂_{t-1|t-1}, w_t = 0); H_t = ∂h/∂x_t at x̂_{t|t-1}; H_v = ∂h/∂v_t at (x̂_{t|t-1}, v_t = 0).

Expand the motion linearization into the linear-Gaussian form (eq. 34): x_t = F_t x_{t-1} + ũ_t + w̃_t, where ũ_t = f(x̂_{t-1|t-1}, u_t, 0) − F_t x̂_{t-1|t-1} is known and plays the role of the control term. The noise w̃_t = F_w w_t is a linear map of a zero-mean Gaussian, so w̃_t ~ N(0, F_w Q_t F_w^T).
Do the same for the observation linearization (eq. 35): z_t = H_t x_t + z̃_t + ṽ_t, where z̃_t = h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0) − H_t x̂_{t|t-1}, and ṽ_t = H_v v_t ~ N(0, H_v R_t H_v^T).

If all random variables are Gaussian, the linearized models give Gaussian transition and measurement densities (eqs. 36–37): p(x_t | x_{t-1}, u_t) = N(F_t x_{t-1} + ũ_t, F_w Q_t F_w^T) and p(z_t | x_t) = N(H_t x_t + z̃_t, H_v R_t H_v^T). Each is written out with its normalizer 1/sqrt(det(2π Σ)) and the quadratic form in the exponent.

Insert these into the Bayes filter recursion (eq. 38). Prediction: bel-bar(x_t) = ∫ p(x_t | x_{t-1}, u_t) bel(x_{t-1}) dx_{t-1} ~ N(x̂_{t|t-1}, P_{t|t-1}). Correction: bel(x_t) = η p(z_t | x_t) bel-bar(x_t) ~ N(x̂_{t|t}, P_{t|t}). The recursion starts from bel(x_0) ~ N(x̂_0, P_0) (eq. 39).

Prediction. The linearized model in step 4 is the linear Kalman filter's motion model, with F_t as the transition matrix, ũ_t as the input term and F_w Q_t F_w^T as the process noise covariance. The linear-KF prediction (derived on the linear_kalman_filter sheet) gives x̂_{t|t-1} = F_t x̂_{t-1|t-1} + ũ_t and P_{t|t-1} = F_t P_{t-1|t-1} F_t^T + F_w Q_t F_w^T. Substituting the definition of ũ_t, the F_t x̂_{t-1|t-1} terms cancel and the mean is x̂_{t|t-1} = f(x̂_{t-1|t-1}, u_t, 0) (eq. 40). The mean goes through the nonlinear f; only the covariance uses F_t.

Correction. The linearized model in step 5 is the linear Kalman filter's observation model, with H_t as the observation matrix, the known offset z̃_t and measurement noise covariance H_v R_t H_v^T. The linear-KF correction (derived on the linear_kalman_filter sheet) gives K_t = P_{t|t-1} H_t^T (H_t P_{t|t-1} H_t^T + H_v R_t H_v^T)^{-1} and P_{t|t} = (I − K_t H_t) P_{t|t-1}. The innovation is z_t − H_t x̂_{t|t-1} − z̃_t. Substituting z̃_t, the H_t x̂_{t|t-1} terms cancel and the innovation is z_t − h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0), so x̂_{t|t} = x̂_{t|t-1} + K_t (z_t − h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0)) (eq. 41).

Additive-noise special case. If the noise enters additively, as in x_k = f(x_{k-1}, u_{k-1}) + w_{k-1} and z_k = h(x_k) + v_k, then F_w = I and H_v = I. The update becomes K_k = P_{k|k-1} H_k^T (H_k P_{k|k-1} H_k^T + R_k)^{-1}, x̂_{k|k} = x̂_{k|k-1} + K_k (z_k − h(x̂_{k|k-1})) and P_{k|k} = (I − K_k H_k) P_{k|k-1}, with H_k = ∂h/∂x at x̂_{k|k-1}. The source also gives the general non-additive form x_k = f(x_{k-1}, u_{k-1}, w_{k-1}), z_k = h(x_k, v_k), which steps 2–9 handle through F_w and H_v.

assumptions.assumption: Near the current estimate, f and h are well approximated by their first-order Taylor expansions.
assumptions.breaks_when: the model curves strongly over the region where the state is uncertain (large P, or a sharply nonlinear f or h). The dropped higher-order terms are then significant, and the propagated covariance no longer describes the true error. The sources note that higher-order EKFs keep more Taylor terms.

assumptions.assumption: The beliefs and noises are Gaussian, so the belief after each step can be summarized by a mean and a covariance.
assumptions.breaks_when: a nonlinear map pushes a Gaussian through f or h. The true result is not Gaussian, for example skewed or multimodal, and keeping only a mean and covariance discards that shape.

assumptions.assumption: The process and measurement noises are zero mean with known covariances Q_t and R_t, and they enter through F_w and H_v evaluated at zero noise.
assumptions.breaks_when: the noise has a bias or a mis-specified covariance. In the non-additive case it also breaks when noise is large enough that linearizing in w and v around zero is poor.

assumptions.assumption: Each Jacobian is evaluated at the current best estimate: F_t at x̂_{t-1|t-1} and H_t at x̂_{t|t-1}.
assumptions.breaks_when: the estimate is far from the true state. The Jacobians then describe the wrong local slope, so the gain and the covariance are computed for a linearization the true state does not follow.

assumptions.assumption: The filter is initialized with bel(x_0) ~ N(x̂_0, P_0). The source suggests x̂_0 = 0 and a small P_0 (< 1e-2).
assumptions.breaks_when: the true initial state is far from x̂_0 while P_0 is small. The filter is then overconfident from the first step, gives new measurements little weight, and linearizes around a wrong point.

failure_modes.signature: The estimate drifts or diverges while P_{t|t} stays small: the reported covariance is overconfident compared with the actual error.
failure_modes.cause: The first-order Taylor expansion drops higher-order terms that matter over the spread of P, so F_t P F_t^T and the gain describe a linear system that does not match the true one.

failure_modes.signature: Updates make the error worse. Innovations z_t − h(x̂_{t|t-1}, 0) stay large or have a consistent bias.
failure_modes.cause: H_t and F_t are evaluated at an estimate far from the truth, so the local slope used for the gain is wrong.

failure_modes.mode: Noise Jacobians omitted in the non-additive case
failure_modes.signature: The filter is miscalibrated: it is overconfident or underconfident, depending on how F_w and H_v scale the noise.
failure_modes.cause: Using Q_t and R_t in place of F_w Q_t F_w^T and H_v R_t H_v^T is only valid when the noise is additive (F_w = I, H_v = I).

failure_modes.signature: The filter barely responds to measurements early on and settles on a wrong state.
failure_modes.cause: P_0 is set small, as the source suggests, while x̂_0 is a poor guess. The gain is near zero, so the correction step does little.

instantiation.why_here: None of agrios_ws's own code computes the Extended Kalman Filter. It runs as two robot_localization nodes, ekf_local and ekf_global, and the project only configures them through src/agrios_bringup/config/ekf_local.yaml and ekf_global.yaml. Both nodes estimate the same 15-entry state. ekf_local fuses only velocities: Vx, Vy and Vyaw from /odom_cov, plus Vyaw from /imu. ekf_global fuses those same velocities and also X and Y from /odometry/gps and Yaw from /rtk/heading. The one library line shown is the covariance-prediction step: it multiplies the covariance by the Jacobian on both sides and adds delta_sec times the configured process noise.

concrete.in_your_project: The 15x1 robot_localization state: X, Y, Z, Roll, Pitch, Yaw, Vx, Vy, Vz, Vroll, Vpitch, Vyaw, Ax, Ay, Az. ekf_local and ekf_global each keep their own copy.
transfer_function_jacobian_ in src/ekf.cpp:436, 15x15. It multiplies estimate_error_covariance_ on the left, and its transpose multiplies it on the right.

The covariance half is estimate_error_covariance_ (15x15) as it stands after the src/ekf.cpp:436 update, which sets it to F P F^T plus delta_sec * process_noise_covariance. The shown lines do not include the mean prediction.

process_noise_covariance, 15x15 and diagonal, with the same values in both nodes: X=0.05, Y=0.05, Z=0.06, Roll=0.03, Pitch=0.03, Yaw=0.06, Vx=0.025, Vy=0.025, Vz=0.04, Vroll=0.01, Vpitch=0.01, Vyaw=0.02, Ax=0.01, Ay=0.01, Az=0.015. The shown line multiplies it by delta_sec before adding it.

Each fused source gives a partial measurement of x_t. In both nodes, /odom_cov (odom0) gives Vx, Vy, Vyaw and /imu (imu0) gives Vyaw. In ekf_global only, /odometry/gps (odom1) gives X, Y and /rtk/heading (imu1) gives Yaw.

For /odom_cov, odom_cov_relay.py:12-16 fills a 6x6 twist covariance (36 entries) that is zero except c[0]=0.05 (vx), c[7]=0.05 (vy) and c[35]=0.02 (vyaw). For /rtk/heading, rtk_sim.py:99 sets orientation_covariance, but the values are not in the lines shown. rtk_sim.py:104-105 sets angular_velocity_covariance[0] and linear_acceleration_covariance[0] to -1.0 (commented 'no gyro' and 'no accel'). rtk_sim.py:79-84 sets a diagonal position_covariance on its NavSatFix, but that message reaches ekf_global only through navsat_transform, and the shown lines don't say what /odometry/gps carries.
Starts as initial_estimate_covariance, 15x15 diagonal with 1e-9 on every entry, in both nodes. Later values are estimate_error_covariance_, which feeds the next src/ekf.cpp:436 prediction.

knobs.means: This is Q_t. src/ekf.cpp:436 multiplies it by delta_sec and adds it to transfer_function_jacobian_ * P * transfer_function_jacobian_^T, so every diagonal entry (X=0.05 through Az=0.015) grows that state's predicted variance by delta_sec times its value on every prediction. The off-diagonals are zero, so this term adds no cross-covariance between states.
Same diagonal values as ekf_global, applied the same way at src/ekf.cpp:436: scaled by delta_sec and added to the propagated covariance.
The starting P, 1e-9 on all 15 diagonal entries, so the filter starts with near-zero uncertainty in every state.
Same as in ekf_global: the starting P is 1e-9 on all 15 diagonal entries.
Selects which state entries the /odom_cov measurement covers in the correction step: Vx, Vy, Vyaw.
Selects X and Y as the state entries the /odometry/gps measurement covers. These are the only position entries either filter fuses.
Selects Vyaw as the only state entry the /imu measurement covers.

Selects Vx, Vy and Vyaw from /odom_cov. In ekf_local no fused source covers X, Y or Yaw.

instantiation.notation: The sheet's F_t is the library's transfer_function_jacobian_ and its P is estimate_error_covariance_. Where the sheet's prediction adds F_w Q_t F_w^T, the shown library line adds delta_sec * process_noise_covariance.
